key_insight: Sharing coefficients can be turned from an ex-post billing rule into day-ahead price signals that steer household demand toward locally useful PV surplus and cut reverse power flow.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical demand-response control layer for low-voltage renewable energy communities, with feeder-aware pricing adding network value by respecting where loads and PV are connected.
method: Compute dynamic sharing coefficients from forecast demand and PV to allocate surplus energy.
Translate allocated energy into household-specific day-ahead price signals.
Use a convex optimization model to reshape loads; compare feeder-aware vs feeder-agnostic community sharing.
evidence_signal: Using measured profiles from 15 households with AC power flow analysis, the approach reduced feeder reverse energy by up to 45.0% and 44.6% on selected days and by 69.0% and 66.3% over the annual window.
watch_item: Performance depends on accurate forecasts, household participation, and communication/optimization infrastructure, so real-world adoption may be sensitive to forecast error and user responsiveness.
paper_title: Sharing Coefficient-Based Price Signals for Demand Response in Renewable Energy Communities
